chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Fadl ibn 'Amir, from Musa ibn al-Qasim al-Bajali, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah ibn A'yun, who said: I saw Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) praying over the small son of Ja'far (peace be upon him), and he said the Takbir over him,

then he said: O Zurarah! Verily, this and its like do not require the prayer (of the deceased). If it were not for the fact that people would say, 'The Hashimites do not pray on the children,' I would not have prayed over him.

Zurarah said: I asked him, 'Was the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) asked about them?' He said: 'Yes, he was asked about them, and he said: Allah knows best what they used to do.'
Then he said: O Zurarah, do you know what His saying 'Allah knows best what they used to do' means?' I said: 'No, by Allah.'

He said: For Allah, the Mighty and High, has the divine will regarding them. That is, when the Day of Judgment comes, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, will hold evidence against seven: the child, the one who died between two prophets, the old man who lived in the time of a prophet but did not have full intellect, the simple-minded, the mentally ill who does not have intellect, the deaf, and the dumb.

So all of these will have evidence held against them by Allah, the Mighty and High, on the Day of Judgment. Allah will send a messenger to them and bring forth a fire for them, and He will say to them: 'Verily, your Lord commands you to jump into this fire.' Whoever jumps into it, it will become cool and a means of peace for him, and whoever disobeys Him will be driven to the fire.

key_terms.الطِّفْلُ: The child (one who dies before age of reason)
key_terms.الْحُجَّةُ: Evidence/proof held against or for someone
key_terms.بَرَدًا وَسَلَامًا: Cool and peace (referring to the fire becoming pleasant)

ai.seo_question: Why do Imams pray over children who die young, and what is the fate of those without full intellect on Judgment Day?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Tawhid elucidates the jurisprudential rationale behind the Imams praying over young children, emphasizing that while not obligatory, it serves to maintain social perception of the Ahl al-Bayt's piety. Theologically, it expands the scope of divine justice to include six categories of those lacking full intellectual capacity or prophetic exposure, introducing the unique concept of a 'voluntary entry' into Hellfire as a means of cooling it for them, thereby reconciling justice with mercy for the innocent.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 5. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar said, on the authority of Fadl ibn `Amir, on the authority of Musa ibn al-Qasim al-Bajali, on the authority of Hammad ibn `Isa, on the authority of Hariz, on the authority of Zurarah ibn A`yun that I saw Abu Ja`far al-Baqir (AS) praying over the small son of Ja`far (AS), so he said the Allhhu Akbar

then said: “O Zurarah! Verily, this and its likes do not require the prayer (of the deceased). If it were not for the fact that people would say “the Hashimites do not pray on the children,’ I would not have prayed.”
Zurarah says: I asked him, “No, by Allah?”

For Allah, the Mighty and High, is the divine will for them. When the Day of Judgement comes, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, will hold evidence over seven: the child, the one that died between the time gap of two prophets, the old man that grasped the era of a prophet while he was not sane, the simple-minded, the mentally ill, the deaf and the dumb.

Then each one of these will seek evidence on Allah, the Mighty and High, on the Day of Judgment. Allah, the Mighty and high, will send to them a messenger, who will make a fire for them and will say: Verily, your Lord has commanded you to jump in it. Thus, whoever jumps init, it will become cool and a means of peace for him, and whoever resists will be drive to the Hell.
